notes:
Shopify store (theme name in source literally reads 'Copy of Summer of Joy ... Rakhi', confirming a live Rakhi/Raksha-Bandhan seasonal campaign at crawl time, Sep 2026). robots.txt has an explicit 'Anthropic AI (Claude) crawler: Allow /' entry, so Tier-1 direct HTTP fetch was used throughout (curl + Node fetch for JSON), no Playwright/Chrome needed. Method: pulled sitemap.xml -> sitemap_collections_1.xml (~600 collection URLs) and grepped for every holiday keyword (diwali, christmas/xmas, halloween, easter, thanksgiving, new-year/nye, holi, rakhi/raksha, eid/iftar/ramadan, valentine, mother/father's day, ganesh/bappa, independence/republic day, women's day). Cross-checked against the homepage nav HTML. For every candidate collection, pulled the full products.json (paginated to true total, not the 250-item page cap) and keyword-scanned titles + product_type facets to content-verify genuineness, per the Mother's-Day false-positive precedent. Total live catalog = 1970 products (confirmed via /collections/all/products.json and the two product sitemaps, ~1971 URLs).

DIWALI: thoroughly checked, as instructed. The umbrella hub 'diwali-with-chumbak' (329 products, 16.7% of catalog) FAILED content verification -- only 3/329 titles were even generically 'festive'-labeled, and the bulk was ordinary bags/watches/drinkware with no Diwali-specific identity, so it was excluded as a row (same failure pattern as christmas-market/mothers-day below). However, three smaller, genuinely curated Diwali sub-collections under that hub DID pass verification and are included: 'Under The Stars' (a-starry-diwali, 30 items, 6/30 titles explicitly starry/diya/lit-themed e.g. 'Under the Stars Diya Gift Set of 6', 'Sitara Owl Wall Hanging'), 'Mithai Platters' (mithai-platters, 9 items, festive sweets-serving platters/thalis), and 'Twinkling Entryway' (twinkling-entryway, 80 items, diya gift sets + tin/soy-wax candles for lighting the entrance, the classic Diwali ritual). og:title tags confirm these are live, customer-facing pages ('Under The Stars', 'Mithai Platters', 'Twinkling entryway'), not orphaned/test URLs.

RAKSHA BANDHAN: strong genuine presence, matching the live 'Rakhi' theme banner. 'Rakhi and Gifts' (rakhi-and-gifts, 106 items) is the site's real gifting hub for the festival (24/106 titles are actual rakhi threads or the 'Threads of Joy' rakhi gift line) and is treated as a grouping/parent row; its subsets 'Rakhis' (rakhi, 7 items -- literal rakhi thread bracelets, e.g. 'Evil-Eye Rakhi', 'Hamsa Rakhi'), 'Rakhi Gifts for Brother' (rakhi-gifts-for-brother, 43 items), and 'Rakhi Gifts for Sister' (rakhi-gifts-for-sister, 31 items) are listed as child rows to avoid double-counting the parent's total. A fourth Rakhi-named collection, 'rakhi-sale' (583 items, 29.6% of the entire catalog), was excluded per the storewide-sale rule -- its name and near-third-of-catalog size mark it as a sitewide discount page riding the Rakhi banner, not a genuine curated Rakhi assortment (sample: 'Jodhpur Love Seat' furniture, generic tote bags).

OTHER FESTIVAL FOUND: 'Bappa Coming Home' (bappa-coming-home, 29 items) is an unambiguous, unmistakably Ganesh-Chaturthi-referencing site-created collection name ('Bappa' = colloquial name for Ganesha in western India) built around elephant-motif merchandise (cushion covers, tumblers, notebooks, brass thali) -- included but FLAGGED because the product tie is via elephant iconography only, not explicit pooja/modak/idol items, so the occasion-specificity is weaker than the Diwali/Rakhi rows.

EXCLUDED AFTER CONTENT-VERIFICATION (this is the Mother's-Day-mistake check applied broadly -- title/URL said the holiday, but the sampled product list was overwhelmingly generic with almost no occasion-specific items):
- Mother's Day ('mothers-day', 231 items, 11.7% of catalog): only 2/231 titles actually say 'Mother's Day' (both just one gift-hamper SKU name); rest is generic bags/mugs/drinkware identical to the normal catalog. Even though it IS a real header-nav link ('Mother's Day Gifts'), it fails the content test, so excluded per the explicit anti-repeat instruction for this exact failure mode.
- Father's Day and its 4 sub-collections ('fathers-day' 73 items 0 keyword matches; 'fathers-day-travel-souvenirs' 2 items; 'fathers-day-dining-kitchen' 7 items; 'fathers-day-decor-living' and 'fathers-day-furniture-storage' both literally 0 products): all generic or empty, no Father's-Day-specific products at all.
- Valentine's Day ('valentine-picks', 87 items): only 5/87 titles were love/couple-themed (mostly generic animal mugs), below the bar applied consistently across all borderline categories.
- Christmas cluster ('christmas-gifts' 80 items 1 match ['Merry Christmas Message Card']; 'christmas-market' 107 items -- 'Tree of Life' is a generic decor print motif, not a Christmas tree; 'once-upon-a-christmas' 51 items same Tree-of-Life reuse; 'christmas-brunches' 111 items 0 matches, plain dining/serveware; 'secret-santa-store' 144 items 0 matches, generic notebooks/mugs; 'santa-picks' 6 items 0 matches; '12-days-of-joy' 250+ items, essentially a broad generic gift catalog): none showed real Christmas-specific product identity (no ornaments, trees-as-decor, santa figurines, snow/reindeer motifs) -- these read as generic gifting/dining pages seasonally relabeled, so Christmas is genuinely absent despite many holiday-named URLs existing.
- Holi ('shop-for-holi', 111 items, 0/111 keyword matches for holi/color/gulal/pichkari): plain cushion covers, coasters, platters -- generic catalog under a Holi label.
- Eid/Ramadan ('iftaar-get-together' 6 items, 'iftar-get-togethers' 29 items, 'iftar-hosting-gifting' 97 items, all 0 matches for eid/ramadan/crescent/lantern): all are plain Marigold-print dinnerware/hosting sets with no Eid-specific imagery.
- Generic cross-holiday hubs 'festive' (130 items, mixes Diwali diyas + Rakhi threads + generic gift cards, only 5 on-theme) and 'festive-gifts' (71 items, similar mix, 7 on-theme) were excluded as unspecific multi-occasion catch-alls rather than single genuine holiday categories -- their few genuine items are already captured via the dedicated Diwali/Rakhi rows above, so nothing is lost by excluding them.
- New Year: exhaustively grepped the full collections sitemap for 'year'/'nye'/'new-year' -- zero matches, genuinely absent.
- Easter, Halloween, Thanksiving: zero matches anywhere in the ~600-URL collections sitemap or homepage nav -- genuinely absent (expected for an India-only retailer).
- Out of the task's holiday scope and excluded without a row: Independence Day ('independence-day', 64 items, patriotic 'People of India' merch, not a decor/gifting festival) and Republic Day ('republic-day-sale', explicit sale page). International Women's Day ('womens-day-gifts', 'womens-day-gifts-1') is also not in the in-scope holiday list given for this task, so excluded (noted for completeness, not evaluated against the content bar).

All included qty figures are exact full-pagination product.json totals (not the single-page 250 cap).
